requirements.statement: The roles and addresses page has the page title 'Consignment addresses - Import notification service - GOV.UK', the caption 'Consignment parties' and the heading 'Consignment addresses'.

requirements.statement: The roles and addresses page lists its sections in this order: Place of origin, Consignor, Consignee, Importer, Place of destination, then the CPH number or the permanent address where one applies.
requirements.why: The prototype and the real page use the same order, which follows the consignment's journey.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-frontend-p9-008 and trace-animals-fit-p14-009 show the same five-party order today, with the CPH row after Place of destination (trace-animals-fit-p14-021).

requirements.statement: Each party section's hint reads: Place of origin 'The address where the animals begin their journey to Great Britain'; Consignor 'This is the sender of the consignment.'; Consignee 'This is the receiver or buyer of the consignment being shipped or transported.'; Importer 'This is usually the same as the consignee. You can select a different person if needed.'; Place of destination 'This is where the animals will be unloaded and accommodated for at least 48 hours. If a health certificate is required, it will show this address.', on the live-animals set's roles and addresses page for every commodity. The germinal-products set's copy of the page keeps the same hints.
requirements.why: Every hint already matches the prototype word for word, so nothing changes. Under ruling sam-2026-10-09 germinal products is a set of its own, so this requirement is the live-animals half.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-frontend-p9-032, -035, -038, -041 and -044 hold the same five hints today, rendered as trace-animals-fit-p14-010 to -014 show.

requirements.statement: The consignor party is named 'Consignor', not 'Consignor or exporter', everywhere the roles and addresses page and the consignor picker name it: the row label, the picker heading, the page title and the visually hidden link text, in English and Welsh. In the same increment the high-risk plants frontend's consignor picker heading and page title and its check-answers label become 'Consignor', in English and Welsh. Internal ids, routes and address-book roles stay as they are in both frontends.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1 names the party 'Consignor' on the page and its picker, and DR1 asked for the same rename; check your answers, the dashboard and the error message already say 'Consignor'. Ruling sam-2026-10-09-pm carries the rename to plants' consignor picker and check-answers label in the same increment (inc-085).

Plants titles and heads its consignor picker 'Consignor or exporter' (repo-plantsfrontend-p6-056, repo-plantsfrontend-p6-081), Welsh 'Anfonwr neu allforiwr' (repo-plantsfrontend-p6-059); its check-answers label changes under ruling-sam-2026-10-09-pm-p3-037.

requirements.why: Design Release 2.1 names the party in each add link.

requirements.statement: An empty Consignee row offers the link 'Add a consignee' to the consignee picker.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1 names the party in each add link.

requirements.statement: An empty Importer row offers the link 'Add an importer' to the importer picker.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1 names the party in each add link.
requirements.deltaNote: Today the link reads 'Add' with ' importer' visually hidden (trace-animals-fit-p14-016).

requirements.statement: An empty Place of destination row offers the link 'Add a place of destination' to the place of destination picker.

requirements.deltaNote: Today the link reads 'Add' with ' place of destination' visually hidden (trace-animals-fit-p14-016).

requirements.statement: Once a party has an address, its row on the roles and addresses page shows the whole address: the name on its own line, then each address line, with the last line ending in a comma and the country name (for example 'Hull, HU9 5PX, United Kingdom').
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1 shows the chosen address in full so the trader can check it without opening check your answers; DR1 asked for the same, and judged that the address being visible is what matters.
requirements.deltaNote: Today an answered row shows only the party's name (trace-animals-fit-p14-062, trace-e2e-p8-064); the country name is already resolved from the stored code (repo-frontend-p9-017).

requirements.statement: Once a party has an address, its add link is replaced by a 'Change' link to that party's picker; using it and picking a different address replaces the copy on the notification.
requirements.why: The prototype and the real page both let the trader re-pick a party from its row.
requirements.deltaNote: trace-animals-fit-p14-063 and repo-tests-p5-019-m1 show the Change link reopening the picker and replacing the copy today.

requirements.statement: Where the CPH section shows, it is headed 'County parish holding (CPH) number' with the hint 'The county parish holding (CPH) number identifies the holding where the animals will be kept.', and once a number is entered it shows the number with a 'Change' link to the CPH number page.
requirements.why: The prototype and the real page already agree on the CPH row's wording and its answered state.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-frontend-p9-020 to repo-frontend-p9-022 and trace-e2e-p8-061 show the same heading, hint and Change link today.

requirements.statement: On the live-animals set's roles and addresses page, the CPH number section shows for every consignment except one whose commodity codes are only horses (0101) or other animals needing a permanent address (01061900). The germinal-products set's page, which shows no CPH number section at all, is this requirement's germinal half, a requirement of its own.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1 lists which commodity codes leave the CPH number out. Ruling sam-2026-10-09 splits this requirement per set and takes the germinal lines out of the live-animals catalogue, so the live-animals set only ever meets the live codes, and it already exempts exactly 0101 and 01061900.
requirements.deltaNote: Today the CPH row is the default and only commodity codes 0101 and 01061900 are exempt (trace-animals-fit-p14-027, repo-frontend-p9-179, repo-frontend-p9-178). The germinal codes 05111000 and 05119985 are still asked today only because the live-animals catalogue holds the 12 germinal lines; taking them out (ruling-sam-2026-10-09-p1-026) is the commodity catalogue's work, not this page's.

requirements.statement: For commodity code 01061900, when at least one selected species needs a permanent address, the roles and addresses page shows a 'Permanent address' section with the hint 'A permanent address is where an animal:' and the bullets 'will permanently reside' and 'can be checked by the Animal and Plant Health Agency (APHA)', and the link 'Add a permanent address'; no other consignment shows it.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1 puts the permanent address among the consignment's addresses for pets; the real page shows no such section today.
requirements.deltaNote: Today a cat consignment's roles and addresses page shows only the five party rows (trace-animals-fit-p14-026). Where the link leads, and the permanent address pages themselves, belong to the cph-permanent-and-contact area.

requirements.statement: When a place of origin has been chosen and the consignor is still empty, the Consignor row offers a 'Same as place of origin' button, styled as a link, beside its 'Add a consignor' link.
requirements.why: The consignor is often the farm of origin; Design Release 2.1 lets the trader reuse it in one press. DR1 asked for the same shortcut.
requirements.deltaNote: Today choosing one party never offers to fill another (trace-animals-fit-p14-073).

requirements.statement: When a consignee has been chosen and the importer is still empty, the Importer row offers a 'Same as consignee' button, styled as a link, beside its 'Add an importer' link.
requirements.why: The importer hint already says it is usually the same as the consignee, yet today the trader has to pick it again; Design Release 2.1 and DR1 both give a shortcut.
requirements.deltaNote: Today the Importer row still reads 'Not added yet' with only an add link after a consignee is chosen (trace-animals-fit-p14-073).

requirements.statement: When a consignee has been chosen and the place of destination is still empty, the Place of destination row offers a 'Same as consignee' button, styled as a link, beside its 'Add a place of destination' link.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1 lets the trader reuse the consignee as the place of destination in one press.
requirements.deltaNote: Today no row offers to copy another (trace-animals-fit-p14-073).

requirements.statement: A same-as button shows only while its source party has an address and its target party has none; only place of origin copies to consignor, and only consignee copies to importer and place of destination.
requirements.why: The shortcut is offered only where it can help, and Design Release 2.1 has no other pairings.

requirements.statement: Pressing a same-as button submits the roles and addresses page's own form, saves on the notification a copy of the source party's record (name, address lines, country and contact details) as the target party, and reloads the page with no success banner, showing the copied address with a 'Change' link and no same-as button. The copy is independent: changing the source party later does not change it, and it is made even when the address is not one the target's picker would offer.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1 fills the row in place with no picker; the real service must persist the copy on the notification like any other pick, and the hub's rows have to sit inside its form for the button to submit it.
requirements.deltaNote: Today the page's form already posts with a crumb and concurrency token (trace-animals-fit-p14-019) and a pick stores a copy of the record (repo-frontend-p9-085, repo-frontend-p9-086), but the summary list sits outside the form (document-dr1-parity-backlog-p6-023).

requirements.statement: Pressing 'Save and continue' on the roles and addresses page never shows an error for empty sections; completeness shows only in the task status.
requirements.why: The prototype and the real page both let the trader move on with sections still empty.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-frontend-p9-027 shows the page's submit redirects without checking any answer today.

requirements.statement: On a new notification's opening run through the journey, 'Save and continue' on the roles and addresses page goes on to the contact address for this consignment page (not the CPH number page), or to the overview when every overview section is already complete. Opened from its overview task, the page returns to the overview on 'Save and continue' (req-1615); under check-your-answers change context it still returns to check your answers.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1 takes the trader on to the next step of the journey, the contact address, rather than to the CPH number, which it reaches only from the page's own CPH row. Ruling sam-2026-10-09 confirms that a page opened from its overview task returns to the overview and removes the criterion that ran Roles and addresses on to the CPH number page.
requirements.deltaNote: Today the page's submit follows the live flow (repo-frontend-p9-026): the opening run goes on to the CPH number page and then the overview (repo-tests-p1-086), and once the overview has been shown it lands on the overview (trace-animals-fit-p14-075). The opening run's next step becomes the contact address page; the overview-opened return is req-1615's change, which this page shares.

requirements.statement: The roles and addresses page ends with a 'Save and continue' button, a secondary 'Save and return to overview' button that saves and goes to the overview, and a 'Cancel and return to overview' link to the overview.
requirements.why: The prototype and the real page give the same three controls on this page, which the overview links to.
requirements.deltaNote: trace-animals-fit-p14-018 shows the same three controls today.

requirements.statement: The 'Roles and addresses' task is complete only when every section shown for the consignment is complete: each party has an address, and the CPH number or permanent address is given where that section shows.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1 counts every section the page shows towards the task, so a cattle notification is not complete without its CPH number.
requirements.deltaNote: Today the task is Complete once the five parties are picked and the page submitted (repo-frontend-p9-028, repo-frontend-p9-004); no today source shows the CPH row counting towards it (trace-animals-fit-p14-081), and the permanent address is not on this page.

requirements.statement: The overview's '5. Consignment parties' section holds the task 'Roles and addresses', with the hint 'Consignor or Exporter, Consignee, Importer and Place of Destination', linking to the roles and addresses page.
requirements.why: The prototype and the real overview already agree on the task's name and hint.
requirements.deltaNote: trace-animals-fit-p14-001 and trace-animals-fit-p14-002 show the same task and hint today.

requirements.statement: Each party picker has the page title '<party> - Import notification service - GOV.UK', the caption 'Consignment parties' directly above an h1 naming the party, and that party's hint from the roles and addresses page as its intro.
requirements.why: The prototype and the real pickers already agree on this, apart from the consignor's name.
requirements.deltaNote: trace-animals-fit-p14-028 to -034 show the same title, caption, heading and intro today.

requirements.deltaNote: repo-frontend-p9-050 and trace-e2e-p9-046 show Back going to the roles and addresses page today.

requirements.statement: Each of the five party pickers (place of origin, consignor, consignee, importer, place of destination) offers 'Add a new address' for its role as a secondary button beside its heading, not as a plain link under the intro; it is still left out in stub mode, where there is no address service to add to. The high-risk plants frontend's consignor and place of destination pickers, which offer no add-address control today, are left without one.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1 presents adding an address as a button beside the heading. Where the button leads is the party-address-add-and-edit area's. Plants has no add-address control to restyle, and ruling sam-2026-10-09-pm leaves plants alone where it has no equivalent; plants traders add a missing consignor in the INS address book first (d-014).

requirements.statement: The consignor, consignee, importer and place of destination pickers each have a search box labelled 'Search' with the hint 'Name, address or country'. The high-risk plants frontend's consignor and place of destination pickers keep the same label and hint.
requirements.why: The prototype and the real pickers already agree on this wording.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-frontend-p9-053 and trace-animals-fit-p14-037 show the same label and hint today. repo-plantsfrontend-p6-001 and repo-plantsfrontend-p6-083 show plants' pickers worded the same.

requirements.statement: The picker's 'Search' label is styled as a medium heading, on the animals party pickers and on the high-risk plants frontend's consignor and place of destination pickers.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1 gives the search label medium heading weight. Ruling sam-2026-10-09-pm gives plants' pickers the same search control in the same increment (inc-086).
requirements.deltaNote: Today the label is small (govuk-label--s; trace-animals-fit-p14-037). Plants' picker chrome is copied from the animals party picker (repo-plantsfrontend-p6-045), its search labelled 'Search' the same way (repo-plantsfrontend-p6-001).

requirements.statement: On the animals party pickers and on the high-risk plants frontend's consignor and place of destination pickers, the search is run by a search icon button beside the box, with the accessible name 'Search', in place of the secondary 'Search' text button; the icon button submits the picker form, so search still works without JavaScript.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1 uses an icon button; DR1 judged that the server-side search must stay as the no-JavaScript fallback, which a non-submitting icon button would lose. Ruling sam-2026-10-09-pm keeps every search a form with a button that submits it, the pickers' search being the server search behind a submitting search button, and gives plants the same control.
requirements.deltaNote: Today search runs from a secondary 'Search' text button that posts the form with action=search (repo-frontend-p9-054, trace-e2e-p9-018). Plants has the same secondary 'Search' text button submitting the form (repo-plantsfrontend-p6-003, repo-plantsfrontend-p6-004).

requirements.statement: With JavaScript, typing in a party picker's search box hides the rows whose name, address lines or country do not contain the text (ignoring case) and updates the results count, with no page reload, on both animals sets' party pickers and on the high-risk plants frontend's consignor and place of destination pickers. It is its own waiting-on-design increment, built as design answers or dropped if design drops it.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1 narrows the list as the trader types and DR1 judged a live filter layered on the server search worth porting, but ruling sam-2026-10-09-pm holds filtering as you type until design answers question 5, in one waiting-on-design increment that also changes plants.
requirements.deltaNote: Today neither frontend's picker carries client-side JavaScript (repo-frontend-p9-070, document-dr1-parity-backlog-p7-051, repo-plantsfrontend-p6-004); search is a server round trip only.
requirements.blockedBy: Design, with the product owner, answers design question 5 (live filtering as the trader types); until then the server search behind its submit button is the whole search (ruling sam-2026-10-09-pm).

requirements.statement: Submitting the picker's search, or opening it with a search in the address, narrows the list on the server to matching addresses and keeps the text in the box; an empty search shows the whole list again. The high-risk plants frontend's consignor and place of destination pickers keep the same server search.
requirements.why: DR1 judged the existing server-side search must stay as the fallback for traders without JavaScript, and the prototype also filters on the server when given a search.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-frontend-p9-055 and trace-e2e-p9-036 to -040 show server-side search keeping its text, and an empty search restoring the list, today. Plants' pickers search on the server the same way (repo-plantsfrontend-p6-067, repo-plantsfrontend-p6-083).

requirements.statement: Each party picker, on both animals sets and on the high-risk plants frontend's consignor and place of destination pickers, lists every address it offers on one page, with no pagination: the page-number links, the Previous and Next links and the hidden page-number field go.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1 shows every address for the role in one table, and DR1 judged one page with no pagination the portable half of its picker; it lands with role filtering, so the list is the role's addresses rather than the whole book. Ruling sam-2026-10-09-pm builds this now (inc-087) and gives plants the same change in the same increment.
requirements.deltaNote: Today the picker shows five addresses a page, cut from 25-record API pages, with GOV.UK pagination (repo-frontend-p9-065 to -072, trace-e2e-p9-032 to -035); the whole book can already be read unpaginated, as the contact picker does (repo-frontend-p9-167). Plants' pickers page five records at a time, with page links carrying q, page and selected (repo-plantsfrontend-p6-007, repo-plantsfrontend-p6-024, repo-plantsfrontend-p6-022).

requirements.statement: The animals party pickers and the high-risk plants frontend's consignor and place of destination pickers no longer show a 'Selected address: <name>' inset: the chosen address is always on screen as its checked row.
requirements.why: The inset exists only because the chosen row could be on another page; with one page it goes, as in Design Release 2.1 and as DR1 judged. Ruling sam-2026-10-09-pm drops the inset now (inc-087), plants included.
requirements.deltaNote: Today the picker restates the choice in a 'Selected address:' inset and carries it across pages in a hidden 'selected' field (repo-frontend-p9-057, repo-frontend-p9-076, trace-e2e-p9-047, trace-e2e-p9-048). Plants shows the same inset and carries the ticked row across pages (repo-plantsfrontend-p6-017, repo-plantsfrontend-p6-070).

requirements.statement: Under the search, each animals party picker and the high-risk plants frontend's consignor and place of destination pickers show the heading 'Select an address' above the results count.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1 heads the list of addresses; DR1 asked for the same heading. Ruling sam-2026-10-09-pm gives plants the same heading in the same increment (inc-086).
requirements.deltaNote: Today the results table has no heading above it; its caption carries the count (document-dr1-parity-backlog-p7-016, trace-animals-fit-p14-039). Plants' table likewise has only a caption (repo-plantsfrontend-p6-008).

requirements.statement: The picker's results count reads 'Showing <visible> out of <total> results', in English and Welsh, and changes as the list is filtered, on the animals party pickers and on the high-risk plants frontend's consignor and place of destination pickers.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1 words the count this way; DR1 asked for the same rewording. Ruling sam-2026-10-09-pm gives plants the same count in the same increment.
requirements.deltaNote: Today the table caption reads 'Showing <shown> of <total> addresses' (repo-frontend-p9-058, trace-e2e-p9-027), Welsh 'Yn dangos <shown> o <total> cyfeiriad' (repo-frontend-p9-089-m1), and says 'addresses' even for one (trace-e2e-p9-028). Plants' caption reads the same 'Showing {shown} of {total} addresses' (repo-plantsfrontend-p6-008, repo-plantsfrontend-p6-008), Welsh 'Yn dangos {shown} o {total} cyfeiriad' (repo-plantsfrontend-p6-049).

requirements.statement: The picker's address table sits inside one fieldset whose legend 'Select an address' is visually hidden, on the animals party pickers and on the high-risk plants frontend's consignor and place of destination pickers.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1 groups the address radios under one legend, so assistive technology announces them as one choice. Ruling sam-2026-10-09-pm gives plants the same fieldset in the same increment.
requirements.deltaNote: Today each row's radio sits in its own form group, with no fieldset or legend for the whole choice (trace-e2e-p9-022). Plants' rows each carry their own small radio with no fieldset around them (repo-plantsfrontend-p6-010).

requirements.statement: The picker lists addresses in a table with a radio column (header 'Select', visually hidden), Name, Address and Country columns, and a last column for the row's action (header visually hidden); each row's radio has the visually hidden label 'Select <name>'. The high-risk plants frontend's consignor and place of destination pickers have the same columns and radio labels.
requirements.why: The prototype and the real picker already agree on the table and its radios.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-frontend-p9-059, repo-frontend-p9-060 and trace-e2e-p9-020 show the same columns and radio labels today. repo-plantsfrontend-p6-009 and repo-plantsfrontend-p6-010 show plants the same.

requirements.statement: The picker's Address column shows each address line on its own line, not joined by commas, on the animals party pickers and on the high-risk plants frontend's consignor and place of destination pickers.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1 prints one line per address line, which reads more easily in a narrow column. Ruling sam-2026-10-09-pm gives plants the same address lines in the same increment.
requirements.deltaNote: Today the Address column joins address lines, town, county and postcode with commas on one line (repo-frontend-p9-061, trace-e2e-p9-024). Plants joins address line 1, line 2, town, county and postcode with commas too (repo-plantsfrontend-p6-011).

requirements.statement: Each picker row ends with a 'View' link that opens that address in the INS address book, carrying a return path that brings the trader back to the same picker. This is the animals pickers' change only: the high-risk plants frontend is not wired to the INS address book, so its pickers keep their 'View details' disclosure.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1 shows an address's details on the address book's own page rather than in an expander; the address book belongs to the INS frontend, so its view page has to honour the return to the animals picker.
requirements.deltaNote: Today each row has a 'View details' disclosure that expands in place with the full record (repo-frontend-p9-062, repo-frontend-p9-063, trace-e2e-p9-026); the tests repo proves it expands without navigating (repo-tests-p5-014).

requirements.statement: Reopening a picker for a party that already has an address picked from the book pre-selects that address's radio; a copy that was edited, or whose record has gone from the book, opens with nothing selected. The high-risk plants frontend's consignor and place of destination pickers already pre-select the saved address, and a saved reference whose record has gone opens with nothing selected.
requirements.why: The prototype pre-selects the current choice, and the real picker already does.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-frontend-p9-073 and trace-animals-fit-p14-070 show the saved address pre-selected today.

requirements.statement: Pressing 'Save and continue' on a party picker with no address chosen shows no error and leaves the party as it was, empty or holding its earlier address. An animals party picker returns to the roles and addresses page; the high-risk plants frontend's consignor and place of destination pickers move on as their save does, to the next page of the journey.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1 lets the trader leave a picker without choosing; completeness is checked by the task status and the review, not by the picker. Ruling sam-2026-10-09-pm gives plants' consignor and place of destination pickers the same lenient blank save in the same increment (inc-086); plants' task status still shows the party as not done.
requirements.deltaNote: Today saving with nothing chosen keeps an address already held (repo-frontend-p9-079), but with none held it re-renders the picker with status 400 and 'Select a <party> from the list' (repo-frontend-p9-080, trace-animals-fit-p14-050 to -054). requirements.statement: Saving a picker with an address that is not in the organisation's book, or has been deleted since the page loaded, saves nothing and re-renders the picker with status 400, an error summary 'There is a problem' and the party's error: 'Select a place of origin from the list', 'Select a consignor from the list', 'Select a consignee from the list', 'Select an importer from the list' or 'Select a place of destination from the list' (and their Welsh), the summary link going to the first address radio, or to the search box when there are no rows. The high-risk plants frontend's consignor and place of destination pickers keep the same refusal of an id the address book does not hold, with 'Select a consignor from the list' or 'Select a place of destination from the list', the message shown above the results table with a visually hidden 'Error:' prefix, and the summary link to the first row's radio or, with no rows, the search box.

requirements.deltaNote: repo-frontend-p9-081 shows an id not in the organisation's book, or soft-deleted, refused with the party error today. repo-plantsfrontend-p6-088, repo-plantsfrontend-p6-019 and repo-plantsfrontend-p6-031 show plants refusing such an id the same way today.

requirements.statement: Outside an amendment, each of the five party pickers (place of origin, consignor, consignee, importer, place of destination) and the CPH number page end with a single primary 'Save and continue' button, with no 'Save and return to hub' button and no cancel link. While amending, their endings are req-1624's.
requirements.why: DR1 ruled this same difference (rule (b)): only pages the overview links to end with the three return controls, and a page reached from another page ends with the primary button alone; the pickers are reached from the roles and addresses page.

requirements.statement: Choosing an address on a picker and pressing 'Save and continue' saves on the notification a copy of that record (the record it came from, name, phone, email and address) and returns to the roles and addresses page, or to check your answers under change context. The roles and addresses page names each party from that copy, never from the address book, including after submission. This copy is the animals frontend's: the high-risk plants frontend keeps saving a reference to the record instead.

requirements.deltaNote: repo-frontend-p9-085, repo-frontend-p9-086 and trace-e2e-p9-044 show the copy saved and the redirect to the roles and addresses page today.

requirements.statement: If saving a picked address fails with a recoverable backend error, the picker re-renders with status 500, the recoverable-error message and the choice still selected. requirements.deltaNote: repo-frontend-p9-088 shows this behaviour today.

requirements.statement: Each party picker, on both animals sets and on the high-risk plants frontend's consignor and place of destination pickers, offers only the organisation's addresses whose roles include that party's role: place of origin, consignor, consignee, importer or place of destination.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1 filters each picker to its role, so a trader is not offered a GB importer as a place of origin; DR1 found the unfiltered list a live defect on all the pickers, and ruling sam-2026-10-09 keeps address roles because DR1 asked for role-filtered pickers. Ruling sam-2026-10-09-pm builds the role-filtered pickers now (inc-087) and gives plants the same change in the same increment.
requirements.deltaNote: Today all five pickers search one undifferentiated book with no address type (repo-frontend-p9-047), so every role offers the same addresses (trace-animals-fit-p14-045). Plants' pickers search the organisation's whole book by search term alone (repo-plantsfrontend-p6-006).

requirements.statement: An address saved with several roles appears on the picker of every party whose role it carries.

requirements.statement: The address book (trade-imports-address-book) holds one or more roles on each address record and lets a frontend list an organisation's addresses for one role, unpaginated and still excluding deleted records; the animals frontend and the high-risk plants frontend each ask for their picker's role. The record's field shape for roles is the address book service's own design, not the prototype's.
requirements.why: DR1 found role filtering needs a typed address record, which no frontend can fake; the address book is one of this programme's repos, so the record shape and the role-aware list are built here. Ruling sam-2026-10-09 keeps address roles (inc-087) and leaves their field shape to the address book. Collecting the roles when an address is saved is the address-book and party-address-add-and-edit areas' work.

requirements.statement: Every address-book read from the animals frontend is made on the server, for the signed-in session's organisation only, carrying that organisation in the Trade-Imports-Organisation-Id header and the request tracing header; with no organisation in the session no read is made. requirements.deltaNote: repo-frontend-p9-155 to repo-frontend-p9-157 show this scoping today.

requirements.deltaNote: repo-frontend-p9-160 and repo-frontend-p9-163 show deleted records kept off the picker today.

The trace gaps they record (no trace of 'Cancel and return to hub' on a picker or the CPH page, no snapshot of two stub-mode pickers) need nothing built.

conflicts.about: Whether the roles and addresses page becomes headed sections with insets, as the prototype draws it, or keeps its summary list.

positions.says: Each section is an h2 heading with its hint below and the chosen address in an inset.
DR1 judged that the requirement is that the address is visible, not that the component matches; a summary list may stay.

The page lists the parties as summary-list rows.

The prototype's headed-section markup is set aside; its address content stands.

The warning reads 'Providing a false address is an act of fraud.'

conflicts.outcome: Ruling sam-2026-10-09-pm ranks first. Built now, on both animals sets and on plants' consignor and place of destination pickers: one page per role with no pagination and no 'Selected address' inset, searched on the server behind a submitting search button (req-593, req-594, req-595), landing with role filtering (req-608). Filtering as you type, which DR1 and the prototype both wanted, is its own waiting-on-design increment, blocked on design question 5 for both animals sets and plants (req-592); the place of origin's as-you-type country filter waits the same way (req-1951). Today's pagination goes in both frontends.

conflicts.about: How the picker's results count is worded.

positions.says: The count reads 'Showing <visible> out of <total> results'.
The table caption reads 'Showing <shown> of <total> addresses'.

conflicts.outcome: The prototype wins by default, and DR1 asked for the same wording; the count moves out of the table caption to sit under the 'Select an address' heading.

conflicts.about: Whether the picker's Address column shows one line per address line or one comma-joined line.

positions.says: The Address column has one line per address line.
The Address column joins the address parts with commas.

conflicts.outcome: The prototype wins by default: one line per address line.

conflicts.about: Whether a picker row shows an address's details through a 'View' link to the address book or a 'View details' expander.

positions.says: Each row has a 'View' link that opens the address in the address book with a return path to the picker.
Each row has a 'View details' disclosure.
View details expands in place, without navigating, so nothing typed or ticked is lost.
The picker 'View' links to the INS address book are animals only, because plants is not wired to the INS address book.

conflicts.outcome: The prototype wins by default: each row gets a 'View' link to the INS address book with a return to the picker. Cross-service behaviour is a constraint the prototype cannot express, but it does not prevent this: the INS frontend is in the programme and must honour the return path. The tests repo's in-place expander test changes with it. Ruling sam-2026-10-09-pm keeps this to the animals pickers: plants' pickers keep their 'View details' disclosure (req-1952).

conflicts.about: What happens when a picker is saved with no address chosen.

positions.says: Submitting with no address chosen shows no error and returns to the roles and addresses page with the section unchanged.
A picker continued with nothing chosen returns to the roles page unchanged.
With nothing selected and no address held, the picker re-renders with status 400 and the party's error.
An id not in the organisation's book, or soft-deleted, is refused with the same party error.
A blank save on plants' consignor and place of destination pickers no longer raises an error.
Saving plants' place of destination with nothing chosen re-shows the page with the party error and status 400.

conflicts.outcome: The prototype wins by default for a blank save: no error, back to the roles and addresses page, party unchanged. The ruling's validation override covers constraints the prototype cannot express, and a blank pick on a draft is not one: the prototype designs it explicitly and its specs assert it. Refusing a record that is not, or is no longer, in the organisation's book is such a constraint, so that refusal and its party errors stay (req-604). Ruling sam-2026-10-09-pm gives plants' consignor and place of destination pickers the same lenient blank save, moving on as their save does, while their refusal of an id the book does not hold stays.

conflicts.about: Whether a party picker ends with 'Save and return to hub' and 'Cancel and return to hub' as well as 'Save and continue'.

positions.says: Under DR1 rule (b) the party pickers adopt the save-actions macro passing false, so they end with the primary button alone.
A select page's buttons are 'Save and continue' and 'Save and return to hub', with a 'Cancel and return to hub' link.
Each picker has 'Save and continue', 'Save and return to hub' and 'Cancel and return to hub'.
Each role picker has two buttons, 'Save and continue' and 'Save and return to hub'.
'Save and return to hub' on a select page saves and goes to the overview.
Save and return to hub on a role picker goes to the overview.
Save and return to hub on a picker saves and goes to the overview.
While amending, a select page shows 'Save and return', 'Save and continue' and a 'Save and return to overview' button.
The address sub-pages offer 'Save and return to hub' and 'Cancel and return to hub'.

conflicts.outcome: DR1 already judged this same difference (rule (b), built as ruled): pages reached from another page end with the primary button alone, and the party pickers are reached from the roles and addresses page. The DR1 judgement overrides the prototype, so the pickers keep 'Save and continue' alone, and the prototype's 'hub' versus 'overview' wording on the pickers falls away with the buttons.

conflicts.about: Whether DR1's blocks on the address pages (the address-space collision block and the typed-record block) keep these differences from being built.

positions.says: Only a DR1 judgement or a real constraint the prototype cannot express overrides the prototype.
Every increment that changes an address-selection page is blocked until the team's address work settles.
The consignment party page increments are blocked for the same reason.
A later ruling blocks all six journey pickers.
inc-056, inc-052, inc-045 and inc-063 were blocked because they touch live address work on the party page.
inc-048, role filtering of the pickers, is blocked as needs-backend.
inc-065, the list heading and count, is blocked by the address-space ruling.
inc-055, one page narrowed as you type, is blocked by the address-space ruling.
inc-056, the same-as shortcuts, is blocked.
inc-052, the whole address on the addresses list, is blocked.
inc-045, the 'Consignor' rename, is blocked.
inc-063, the named add links, is blocked.
inc-047 and inc-048 are blocked, or deferred pending the address-book epic.
inc-064, the full-width picker, is blocked because address work in this space would collide.
None of the blocked rows records a decision on the difference itself.

conflicts.outcome: The sam-2026-10-07 ruling ranks first. DR1's blocks defer work for collision or dependency reasons and record no judgement on the differences themselves (document-dr1-parity-backlog-p6-054), so they do not override the prototype. The typed address record they waited on is built in this programme, which includes trade-imports-address-book. DR1's judgements inside those rows (the address must be visible; keep the server search as the no-JavaScript fallback) still apply.

conflicts.about: What the role-filtered pickers offer for address-book records saved before addresses carried roles.

positions.says: A picker lists only addresses whose types include the section's role.
Filtering on a guess would hide addresses the trader legitimately wants.
Plants' pickers search the organisation's whole book by search term alone, with no role.

conflicts.outcome: Each party picker filters typed address-book records by its role, as Design Release 2.1 does (prototype-dr2-1-source-p8-063); an existing record with no role yet is offered on every party picker until it is given one, in the compose stack and in CDP alike, because DR1's inc-048 judgement (document-dr1-parity-backlog-p6-051) rules out hiding addresses the trader legitimately wants on a guess, and records saved before roles existed are a persistence constraint the prototype cannot express. The stub-mode records are each given roles so stub mode shows the filtering. Ruling sam-2026-10-09-pm gives plants' consignor and place of destination pickers the same role filtering, with untyped records still shown everywhere (ruling-sam-2026-10-09-pm-p3-040).

conflicts.about: Whether the place of origin picker searches by country with transit-country wording or uses the free-text search the other pickers use.

positions.says: The place of origin picker searches by country: label 'Enter a country', hint 'Enter each country that the consignment will travel through', placeholder 'Search for a country'.
Every picker's search is labelled 'Search' with the hint 'Name, address or country'.

The place of origin picker's label, hint and placeholder are built now, and its country search is an autocomplete over a native select, or a plain select, with a button that submits the chosen country so the server narrows the rows.
The place of origin rows filtering as the trader types wait on design, for both sets.
The place of origin country search is a client-side widget with an unnamed input, a hidden results list labelled 'Country search results' and its own live region.
The picker search uses custom page classes and an app-commodity-search widget for the country search.

conflicts.outcome: Ruling sam-2026-10-09-pm ranks first. The prototype's label 'Enter a country', hint and placeholder 'Search for a country' are built now as drawn (req-621 to req-623). The country search is the real frontend's accessible autocomplete over a native select of MDM's countries, with a button that submits the chosen country so the server narrows the rows (req-624): the ruling allows a plain select, but it also builds the placeholder now, which only the autocomplete can show, and the goal puts every search box on that component. The prototype's own country widget and its custom announcements are set aside, and its filtering as you type waits on design (req-1951). Ruling sam-2026-10-09-pm leaves rolling the component out to more screens to EUDPA-635 (ruling-sam-2026-10-09-pm-p1-022) but names inc-089's country search as one that may use it (ruling-sam-2026-10-09-pm-p1-026), so this picker is not a roll-out; how the box looks beyond the prototype's label, hint and placeholder is the component's (ruling-sam-2026-10-09-pm-p1-020).

conflicts.about: Whether the consignor party is named 'Consignor' or 'Consignor or exporter'.

positions.says: The consignor section is headed 'Consignor', covering the exporter too.
The consignor party is titled 'Consignor or exporter'.
The hub's party roles include 'Consignor or exporter'.
The rename also changes plants: the consignor picker's heading, title and check-answers label, in English and Welsh.
Plants' consignor page is titled and headed 'Consignor or exporter'.

conflicts.outcome: The prototype wins by default, and DR1 asked for the same rename: 'Consignor' on the row, picker heading, page title and hidden link text, English and Welsh, with the id, route and address-book role unchanged. The overview task hint 'Consignor or Exporter, ...' stays, as the prototype keeps it too. Ruling sam-2026-10-09-pm carries the rename to plants' consignor picker heading, page title and check-answers label in the same increment.

conflicts.about: What makes the 'Roles and addresses' task complete.

positions.says: The task is complete only when every section shown for the consignment is complete.
The task shows Complete once all five parties are picked and the page is submitted.

conflicts.outcome: The prototype wins by default: every shown section, the CPH number or permanent address included, must be complete.

conflicts.about: How the picker's search label and button look.

positions.says: The search label is medium-heading styled and the search runs from an icon button with aria-label 'Search'.
The search label is small and a secondary 'Search' text button sits next to the field.
Plants' consignor and place of destination pickers get the same search control.

conflicts.outcome: The prototype wins by default on appearance: a medium label and an icon button named 'Search'. The button submits the form, per DR1's no-JavaScript judgement (c-094). Ruling sam-2026-10-09-pm gives plants' consignor and place of destination pickers the same label and button.
